findings.issue_text: [BUG] The ClientRemovedEvent branch retained behind the new ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ gate calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), and the V2 implementation this diff activates under that same flag (ClientPermissionsV2.java:192-195) implements setPermissionsEnabled by throwing UnsupportedOperationException. With the feature enabled, deleting any client fires ClientRemovedEvent into ProviderEventManager.publish, which has no exception handling; when the management() call resolves to the V2 evaluator the UnsupportedOperationException propagates, rolls back the store removal and returns 500 on the delete — the diff's own testManageAllClients delete step sits on exactly this path; even in the best case (V1 routing) the diff ships an evaluator that disavows the cleanup its own listener performs, leaving per-client 'Clients' resources orphaned on every client deletion.

[BUG] canExchangeTo is overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException while remaining on the ClientPermissionEvaluator surface whose V1 twin is the token-exchange permission check — this same file's dead getEvaluationContext (lines 258-271) is the verbatim copy of that V1 exchange evaluation context (ClientModelIdentity + kc.client.id attribute). Any token-exchange permission evaluation routed to V2 gets an UnsupportedOperationException instead of a permit/deny decision, so exchanging tokens to a target client fails with a 500 rather than a 403 whenever the V2 evaluator serves that path.

[ADVISORY] getEvaluationContext is dead code — a private method with no call sites (its only conceivable consumer canExchangeTo throws), sitting alongside the never-used logger field (line 51) and the unused static import AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE (line 46). The next maintainer implementing V2 token-exchange support must reverse-engineer whether this half-wired evaluation context is load-bearing; deleting it removes ~15 lines plus three imports with zero behavior change.

[ADVISORY] The all-clients fallback inside hasPermission(ClientModel, String) invokes the get-or-create getResourceTypeResource from within a boolean permission check, and AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource is not synchronized, so the first canView/canManage on any client persists a new 'Clients' resource row from a read path. Client list/view endpoints perform resource-store writes during permission evaluation, and two concurrent first evaluations both miss findByName and create duplicate 'Clients' type resources, after which the findByName lookup in hasPermission(String) (line 244) resolves an arbitrary duplicate so all-clients permissions silently stop applying.

[ADVISORY] canMapClientScopeRoles and the new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope added to the Clients resource type have zero test coverage: none of the five client tests added in PermissionClientTest.java grants that scope or exercises any operation gated by it. A regression in the client-scope role-mapping wiring — e.g. a scope-name mismatch between the schema registration and the endpoint's permission check — ships green, so an admin granted map-roles-client-scope gets 403s with no test failing.

[BUG] The ClientRemovedEvent cleanup branch that this diff edits still calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), but the same diff routes MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() to ClientPermissionsV2 whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException and no other code in the diff removes per-client 'Clients' resources, so the delete-client cleanup requirement is dropped for V2. With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled, deleting any client either dispatches to ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled and aborts the whole client-removal operation with UnsupportedOperationException propagated through the event publish (500/rollback on every client delete), or the listener resolves to the legacy evaluator whose cleanup only touches the legacy resource store while V2 per-client resources (created by AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveClient/getOrCreateResource under the admin-permissions resource server) and their attached scope permissions are never deleted — stale resources accumulate unboundedly and getClientsWithPermission re-evaluates every one of them on each client listing by a non-admin-role user. No test in the diff creates a per-client Clients permission and then deletes that client (testManageAllClients only deletes a client covered by a type-level grant), so neither the throw path nor any cleanup behavior is verified.

[ADVISORY] canExchangeTo and exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException('Not supported in V2') while remaining on the retained ClientPermissionEvaluator interface, and the new Clients resource type defines no token-exchange scope, so the V1 fine-grained token-exchange capability is silently dropped with no replacement, no documented limitation, and no verification. The diff adds no test asserting the V2 behavior of canExchangeTo (the fully-shown PermissionClientTest contains no exchange test), and the same pattern covers isPermissionsEnabled (187-190), resource (197-200) and getPermissions (202-204); any consumer of the public evaluator interface that runs under the feature-enabled V2 wiring — including existing token-exchange permission checks and the per-client permission-management REST surface — receives an unhandled UnsupportedOperationException (500) instead of a permission decision, and admins in V2 realms cannot configure or query these permissions at all.

[ADVISORY] The new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope and its canMapClientScopeRoles override are shipped with zero test coverage: the complete PermissionClientTest rewrite (all hunks shown before the diff moves to PermissionRESTTest) grants and asserts MANAGE, CONFIGURE, VIEW, MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, but MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE appears in no test and is absent from the test file's static imports (lines 22-27 of the diff). A regression in this override — e.g. a copy-paste of canMapCompositeRoles' scope constant, which sits directly above it — ships undetected, and the client-scope role-mapping operations gated by canMapClientScopeRoles will 403 for admins who were legitimately granted map-roles-client-scope (or, in the inverse direction, over-grant); testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient grants Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE) and thereby proves the sibling scopes work while leaving this one unexercised.

[ADVISORY] hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) evaluates only the per-client resource whenever one exists and never consults the type-level 'all clients' grant, contradicting the diff's own javadoc on canManage/canConfigure/canView ('For V2 only: Also if the caller has a permission to ... MANAGE all clients') and creating an asymmetry with canView(client), which short-circuits on the type-level canView() check before the per-client lookup. An admin who grants a user MANAGE on all clients and later creates any per-client Clients permission for client X (even granting a different scope or a different user) silently revokes that user's type-level MANAGE/CONFIGURE/MAP_ROLES grants on X — view still works via the canView() short-circuit but manage stops — and no test in the diff creates both a type-level and a per-client Clients permission to pin the intended precedence, so integrators following the added javadoc will compose grants that silently deny.

[ADVISORY] resolveClient's two-step resolution (internal id first, then human-readable clientId fallback) and its null path are completely unverified: no test in the diff creates a Clients permission using a client's clientId string, and none covers a nonexistent or foreign-realm client id where resolveClient returns null and getOrCreateResource falls into its name == null branch. The acceptance criterion for the fallback lookup the diff adds is missing — an admin creating a permission with the clientId instead of the internal UUID (the natural thing to copy from the console) gets an untested resolution path; likewise a typo'd or deleted client id reaches the untested name==null branch of getOrCreateResource and yields either a silently-created permission that can never match any client (201 for garbage input) or an unhandled server error, instead of a validated 4xx.

[ADVISORY] ClientPermissionsV2 ships dead code: the private getEvaluationContext(authorizedClient, token) method has zero call sites (canExchangeTo throws instead of using it), the declared Logger (line 51) is never used, and the static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE (line 46) is unused. Deleting getEvaluationContext plus its only-purpose imports (ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext, EvaluationContext), the unused TOKEN_EXCHANGE import, the Scope import and the logger removes ~15 lines with no behavior change; leaving them in place falsely signals that V2 wires token-exchange evaluation and invites a future edit to resurrect the dead helper rather than design the V2 exchange behavior deliberately.

[ADVISORY] The three near-identical permission-scan loops (hasPermission(ClientModel,String) at ~206, hasPermission(String) at ~237, hasGrantedPermission at ~277) are copy-pasted with already-observed drift: the realmResourceServer() null-check exists in the first two but not in hasGrantedPermission, and the policyStore.findByResource(...).isEmpty() type-resource guard exists only in the per-client variant. The next change to grant matching — adding a second expected scope, decision caching, or a scope-name variant — must be replicated in three hand-maintained places, and the existing drift shows the copies have already diverged (hasGrantedPermission re-fetches root.realmResourceServer() and dereferences it unguarded, surviving only because its single caller checks first); extracting one shared evaluate(resource, scope) helper deletes the drift and two of the three copies.

[ADVISORY] The PR gates the global role/client/group permission-cleanup listener behind Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ — an unrelated behavioral change smuggled into a PR whose stated intent is only adding a Client resource type and scopes to the authorization schema. Realms that created fine-grained permissions while the feature was enabled and later run with the feature disabled (profile change, config rollback, upgrade drift) silently stop cleaning authorization resource servers on role/client/group deletion; the stale permission data resurrects as live grants over deleted entities when the feature is re-enabled, and the semantic change hides inside a hunk that reindents every line so whitespace-insensitive review tooling shows no gate at all.

[ADVISORY] The PR introduces persisted per-client Clients-typed authorization resources (read via resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId())) but ships no cleanup when a client is deleted — the designated hook, the ClientRemovedEvent listener's clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client,false), dispatches either to this V2 override that unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException or to the V1 implementation that only deletes per-client resource servers the V2 model never creates, so orphans are never removed in either dispatch. Every client deleted in an FGAP-enabled realm leaves an orphaned resource plus its scope permissions in the realm resource server; the orphans surface as ghost entries in the authz admin API and console and are re-scanned and policy-evaluated by getClientsWithPermission on every filtered client list, accumulating without bound.

[ADVISORY] ClientPermissionsV2 replaces the entire V1 permission-management surface (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, the mapRoles*/managePermission/configurePermission/viewPermission Policy getters, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) with unconditional throw new UnsupportedOperationException instead of a designed de-scoping response, while the admin REST endpoints these evaluator methods back remain live. Administrators on FGAP-enabled realms using the existing client management/permissions endpoints (legacy console, provisioning scripts) and any token-exchange flow that consults canExchangeTo receive raw 500 Internal Server Errors rather than a controlled 4xx or feature-gated response.

[BUG] canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles evaluate only explicit map-roles grants and drop the MANAGE_CLIENTS coarse-role fallback that the same class's canManage(client), canManageClientScopes and canView overrides all retain, so an administrator holding the manage-clients role is denied client role mapping in V2 realms. Realm administrators with the manage-clients role get 403 on client role-assignment and composite-role endpoints that gate on these evaluators — a silent reversal of V1 semantics where manage-clients sufficed — and no test in the diff exercises the coarse-role path through these methods, so the narrowing ships unverified.

[ADVISORY] getEvaluationContext is dead code — no method in ClientPermissionsV2 calls it because the token-exchange methods it was written to support were stubbed to throw — and the TOKEN_EXCHANGE static import (line 44), the never-used Logger field (line 49), and the ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext imports exist only to serve this abandoned half-implementation. The next maintainer of the exchange-permission path must reverse-engineer whether token-exchange support was meant to ship, or wires the dead scaffolding in believing it is live; dead security-adjacent code in a permission evaluator also misleads audits of the effective permission surface.

[ADVISORY] The diff contradicts itself on who can enumerate clients: the canList/requireList javadoc added here defines listing as canView() or QUERY_CLIENTS/QUERY_USERS (and the shipped evaluator returns false for a caller holding only a type-level MANAGE grant), yet testManageAllClients in the same diff asserts that exact caller lists all clients — behavior nothing in this diff provides. Either the added test is red, or the client-listing endpoint bypasses the documented canList contract, leaving an undocumented widening of client enumeration; a maintainer implementing or auditing the list endpoint against this javadoc enforces the wrong set of list-capable principals on a security boundary.

[ADVISORY] Three hand-maintained copies of the 'granted permissions carry scope X' loop exist (hasPermission(ClientModel,String) here, hasPermission(String), and hasGrantedPermission) and already show textual drift — two match via Arrays.asList(scope).contains(s), the third via scope.equals(s). The next change to scope matching (name normalization, case handling) applied to one copy silently diverges grant decisions between the per-client, all-clients and list-filter paths; a single hasScope(Collection<Permission>, String) helper deletes ~12 lines and the drift site.

[ADVISORY] canManageClientScopes, canManage(ClientScopeModel) and canView(ClientScopeModel) evaluate the Clients-typed all-clients resource, so a permission whose resource type is 'Clients' silently governs realm client-scope entities — a distinct entity kind that has no resource type in this schema. An operator applying least privilege by granting manage on all clients unknowingly grants create/delete over realm client scopes, whose defaults are inherited by every client in the realm — the grant's reach exceeds what its named resource type advertises, and the schema enforces no invariant tying a permission to the entity kind it governs.

[ADVISORY] The by-clientId fallback branch of resolveClient (getClientByClientId) is exercised by no test in this diff — every visible test passes internal IDs — so the normalization contract that the resource be named by the internal ID (matching ClientPermissionsV2's findByName(server, client.getId()) lookup) ships unverified. A regression in resolveClient that returns the raw clientId as the resource name silently denies every per-client grant (hasPermission falls through to the all-clients type resource and returns false), and no test in the suite fails to catch it.

[ADVISORY] The new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope and its evaluator entry point canMapClientScopeRoles ship with zero coverage — no visible test in the diff grants or asserts that scope anywhere. The map-roles-client-scope capability ships unverifiable: a typo or mis-wiring in the scope name silently denies (or over-grants) client-scope role mapping with no failing test, leaving the scope as inert surface until an operator discovers it does nothing.

[BUG] canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles and canMapClientScopeRoles are permission-only overrides that drop the AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS role short-circuit that every other method in this same class retains (canManage(client) line 66, canManageClientScopes line 107, canView via canViewClientDefault), breaking the V2 formula of 'static role OR fine-grained permission' for exactly these three checks. In any realm running the V2 evaluator, an admin holding the static manage-clients role (including full realm-admin) gets 403 from requireMapRoles when mapping that client's roles to a user, adding composite roles, or adding client-scope roles — operations V1 granted to manage-clients holders; the new tests only exercise the fine-granted 'myadmin' user and never a manage-clients admin, so the suite cannot catch it.

[BUG] The removal-cleanup listener is guarded by Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) while the evaluator returned by management() is the V2 subclass selected by the separate V2 feature switch, so in a deployment with both features enabled the guard passes and line 92 calls MgmtPermissionsV2.clients().setPermissionsEnabled, whose ClientPermissionsV2 override throws UnsupportedOperationException. With both feature flags on, DELETE /admin/realms/{r}/clients/{id} fires ClientRemovedEvent into the synchronous listener, the V2 stub throws, the exception propagates out of the event publish, and every client removal in the realm fails with a 500; the test suite passes only because its config keeps ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ off.

[BUG] getClientsWithPermission runs a full policy evaluation per resource inside the resourceStore.findByType callback (hasGrantedPermission → root.evaluatePermission at lines 274-276), an N+1 evaluation loop over every Clients-type resource with no batching, caching, or limit. The client-list flow that filters by per-client permissions (the diff's own tests show findAll() returning only permitted clients) performs one complete authorization-engine evaluation — each resolving and running its policy set against the user/role stores — per permission-bearing client resource in the realm; a realm with hundreds of per-client permissions turns every admin Clients-page load into hundreds of sequential evaluations, the exact profile that got the V1 feature disabled by default for performance.

[BUG] canExchangeTo is overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException while remaining on the shared ClientPermissionEvaluator surface that the token-exchange flow invokes, and the new Clients resource type (AdminPermissionsSchema line 67) omits any token-exchange scope, so V1's per-client token-exchange grant has no representation in the V2 schema at all. Client-to-client token exchange in a realm where the fine-grained exchange check is active hits the throwing stub and surfaces a raw 500 instead of a grant/deny decision; wherever the check is instead skipped, the V1 policy restriction on exchange silently disappears so any client may exchange — the operator gets either a crash or an unguarded bypass with no policy-governed middle.

[ADVISORY] Eleven working V1 methods (exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, mapRolesCompositePermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) are replaced by raw UnsupportedOperationException throws with no feature gate, HTTP status mapping, or replacement path on the shared evaluator interface. The existing admin API surface that manages per-client fine-grained permissions — e.g. the client management-permissions toggle endpoints (GET/PUT /clients/{id}/management-permissions, which call isPermissionsEnabled/getPermissions/setPermissionsEnabled) — turns from working responses into unhandled 500s the moment the V2 evaluator is active; operators and the admin console get server errors instead of a 4xx 'not supported in V2'.

[BUG] The diff introduces per-client permission resources (AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creating Clients-type resources named by client ID) but provides no cleanup when a client is deleted: the only removal hook, the ClientRemovedEvent listener, is feature-gated off in V2 deployments by this same diff, and the V2 setPermissionsEnabled override throws instead of deleting anything. Every client that ever had a fine-grained permission leaves an orphaned Resource plus its scope-permission rows in the admin resource server after deletion; orphans accumulate unboundedly, still surface in the global scope-permission listing the tests iterate, and are re-evaluated on every getClientsWithPermission list request forever.

[ADVISORY] ClientPermissionsV2 carries dead V1 skeleton code: getEvaluationContext (lines 262-272) has no caller since canExchangeTo now throws, the static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE (line 46) is unused, and the logger field (line 51) is never written to. The next maintainer debugging token-exchange authorization reads an apparently-live evaluation-context path that can never execute, and the copied import/field suggest exchange support exists when it does not; deleting the method plus both unused declarations removes ~15 lines with zero behavior change.

[ADVISORY] The granted-scope matching loop is pasted three times (hasPermission(ClientModel,String) lines 224-232, hasPermission(String) lines 249-257, hasGrantedPermission lines 276-283) and the copies have already drifted: two match via Arrays.asList(scope).contains(s), the third via scope.equals(s). Any future change to how granted scopes are matched (e.g. parameterized scopes or prefix matching) must be applied in three private copies that give no compile error when missed, so the three permission-check paths can silently disagree on what counts as granted.

[BUG] ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException while this same diff's AdminPermissions ClientRemovedEvent handler (AdminPermissions.java lines 89-91, also in this diff) calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), so the PR ships no configuration in which deleting a client removes its permission resources. In any deployment where AdminPermissions.management() resolves to MgmtPermissionsV2 while the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ gate on the listener passes, deleting any client throws UnsupportedOperationException during event dispatch and the delete fails/rolls back (the V1 contract that ClientRemovedEvent cleans up client permissions is destroyed); where the gate keeps the listener dormant, the per-client 'Clients' resource created via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource is silently orphaned, so getClientsWithPermission iterates stale resources and the authorization store accumulates garbage with no removal path.

[BUG] canExchangeTo and exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException, deleting the token-exchange permission path that V1 serves, while the new Clients resource type omits the token-exchange scope so no V2 grant can ever replace it. With the V2 admin permissions feature active, the client-to-client token-exchange permission check throws an unhandled exception (500 on the token endpoint) instead of evaluating or denying; a realm moving from V1 fine-grained permissions loses documented, working token-exchange behavior with no scope in the new schema to re-grant it and no accepted alternative in the diff.

[ADVISORY] The whole V1 per-client permission-management surface (managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, mapRolesCompositePermission, isPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, resource) is kept as public API but stubbed to throw, with no feature-gating of the REST/console endpoints that call these methods. Operators who enable the V2 feature and open a client's Permissions tab (or invoke the V1 permission-management REST endpoints) get unhandled 500 responses rather than a feature-appropriate 4xx or a disabled surface, because nothing in the diff turns those endpoints off under V2.

[ADVISORY] Dead token-exchange scaffolding is left in the shipped file: the private getEvaluationContext method has no caller once canExchangeTo throws, the static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE (line 46) is unused, and the logger field (line 51) is never read. Maintainers reading the class are misled into believing V2 token-exchange evaluation is implemented or imminent; all three artifacts are deletable with zero behavior change, and the next token-exchange change starts from stale, misleading scaffolding.

[ADVISORY] The permission/scope matching loop is hand-duplicated three times in one new class (hasPermission(ClientModel,String) lines 225-233, hasPermission(String) lines 250-258, hasGrantedPermission lines 277-284) and the copies have already diverged in style (Arrays.asList(scope).contains(s) vs scope.equals(s)). Any future change to scope-matching semantics (e.g., matching a scope set or normalizing scope names) must be applied in three places; missing one yields inconsistent permission decisions between canManage/canView/canMapRoles and getClientsWithPermission for the same grant, with no test forced to catch the divergence.

[ADVISORY] canMapClientScopeRoles (the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope this diff adds to the Clients schema) is the only new Clients scope with no test anywhere in the diff, while every sibling scope (MANAGE, CONFIGURE, VIEW, MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE) gets end-to-end assertions in PermissionClientTest. A regression in the scope constant or in the wiring of canMapClientScopeRoles to the client-scope role-mapping endpoints passes CI silently, leaving admins granted map-roles-client-scope with a silent no-op (or an over-grant) on those endpoints.

[BUG] ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, and the ClientRemovedEvent handler this same diff wires up (AdminPermissions.java:91 calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) under the new Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) gate) invokes it for every client deleted while the feature is enabled — the exact state in which MgmtPermissionsV2 serves clients() with this V2 evaluator. With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled, deleting any client throws UnsupportedOperationException from the event listener: DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id} returns 500 and the removal rolls back (leaving the client undeletable) or leaves dangling V2 authorization resources, and the diff's own testManageAllClients delete step cannot succeed.

[BUG] canExchangeTo unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException while the method remains on the retained ClientPermissionEvaluator surface whose V1 token-exchange authorization path (the runtime check that a client may exchange a token into a target client, evidenced by the copied-but-unused getEvaluationContext helper at line 246) still calls it whenever V2 is the active evaluator. In realms with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (and token-exchange) enabled, a cross-client token exchange that previously evaluated the token-exchange permission now crashes with a 500 on the protocol endpoint instead of returning a grant/deny decision.

[ADVISORY] getClientsWithPermission runs a full policy evaluation (hasGrantedPermission → root.evaluatePermission, each hitting the policy store) for every Clients-type resource on each call, making the client-list filtering path cost O(number of permission-bearing clients) evaluations per HTTP request. An admin holding per-client grants in a realm where hundreds of clients carry fine-grained permissions pays hundreds of policy evaluations on every admin-console client list, so list latency grows linearly with the number of permissioned clients — the feature's primary use case.

[ADVISORY] The deny path of hasPermission(ClientModel, String) mutates persistent state: when the per-client resource is absent it calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource (get-or-create), so a permission check — including one that ends in deny — creates the 'Clients' type resource in the authorization store. Operators see authorization-store rows written by read-only admin operations (e.g., an ungranted admin's first GET on any client in a fresh realm triggers the creation), so permission evaluation is not side-effect-free and any read-only or replicated evaluation context is broken by a write during a check.

[BUG] The ClientRemovedEvent branch calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false), which this same PR wires to ClientPermissionsV2 (via MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()) whose setPermissionsEnabled override throws UnsupportedOperationException, so client-removal permission cleanup cannot execute in exactly the configuration (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled, V2 active) that every test in this diff runs under. Deleting any client with fine-grained permissions under V2 either throws inside the event listener (failing DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id} with a 500 if the exception propagates) or, if the event dispatch swallows it, silently orphans the client's authorization resource; testManageAllClients only removes 'newClient', a client with no permission resource, so no test in the diff removes a permissioned client and the broken cleanup path ships undetected.

[BUG] testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient grants MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE and CONFIGURE in a single permission before asserting the role-mapping operations succeed, so the assertions cannot attribute authorization to any specific scope — if canMapCompositeRoles in ClientPermissionsV2 checked MAP_ROLES or CONFIGURE instead of MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, this test still passes. A scope-constant swap in the three near-identical V2 overrides (canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles) ships with a green suite: the discriminating case — grant MAP_ROLES only and assert addComposites still returns 403 — is absent, so composite-role administration gets wrongly granted or wrongly denied in production with no CI signal.

[ADVISORY] The new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope and the canMapClientScopeRoles override are covered by no test in the diff's test changes (checked: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/AbstractPermissionTest.java, PermissionClientTest.java, PermissionRESTTest.java, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java — PermissionClientTest's imported scopes are exactly CONFIGURE, MANAGE, MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, VIEW, and no test grants MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE or calls a client scope-mapping endpoint). A copy-paste error in this one-liner sibling of canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles — the likeliest regression in this exact trio of new scopes — makes the admin client scope-mapping endpoints (POST /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/scope-mappings) grant or deny the wrong principals with no failing test.

[ADVISORY] The admin-role fast paths of the new V2 evaluator — canManage(ClientModel)'s root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS), canManage()'s super.canManage(), and canView()'s canViewClientDefault() — are exercised by no test in the diff, because every visible test authenticates as 'myadmin', a user with no admin roles who is granted only type/resource permissions. A regression that breaks the MANAGE_CLIENTS/VIEW_CLIENTS role bypass under V2 keeps the entire suite green while locking realm administrators out of all client management on any realm with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled; only the role-less permission path is verified.

[ADVISORY] The new resolveClient fallback branch (session.clients().getClientByClientId(realm, id), lines 179-181) is never tested — every test in the diff addresses client permissions by internal id (myclient.getId()), while the analogous username fallback for USERS is covered by PermissionRESTTest.resourcesTest, and no test creates a client permission addressed by clientId. If the fallback or the new CLIENTS branch in getOrCreateResource (lines 92-93) regresses, creating a client permission by clientId resolves a null name and the request fails for any caller that addresses clients by clientId (the natural analog of the tested username path), and nothing in CI catches it.

[ADVISORY] The V2 overrides gating realm-level client-scope administration — canManageClientScopes(), canManage(ClientScopeModel) and canView(ClientScopeModel) — are covered by no test in the diff: the visible tests only touch per-client default/optional client-scope endpoints and never the /admin/realms/{realm}/client-scopes CRUD endpoints these methods authorize. A wrong gate on realm client-scope create/update/delete under V2 (e.g., canView(ClientScopeModel) or canManageClientScopes evaluating the wrong scope or role constant) ships undetected, and operators cannot tell from the suite whether client-scope administration is authorized correctly under the new model.

[ADVISORY] The false-branch of the newly added Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) guard — skipping the RoleRemoved/ClientRemoved/GroupRemoved permission cleanup entirely — is triggered by no test in the diff, since every test runs on the feature-enabled KeycloakAdminPermissionsServerConfig. Realms where fine-grained permissions were created and the feature was then disabled now silently leak authorization resources on every role/client/group removal (before this gate the cleanup ran unconditionally), and the suite gives no signal about the changed behavior of feature-disabled deployments.

[ADVISORY] The private getEvaluationContext(authorizedClient, token) helper is dead code — no method in the class calls it, since the V1 canExchangeTo that used it is overridden to throw — and the unused logger field (line 51) plus the ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext/EvaluationContext imports, the unused Scope import, and the unused static TOKEN_EXCHANGE import exist only as leftover V1 scaffolding. The next reader of V2 concludes client-identity token-exchange evaluation exists here when it actually throws, and the next change to this class must first disentangle which imports, the logger, and the helper are live; deleting the method plus its now-unused imports and field removes ~15 lines with zero behavioral impact.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The ClientRemovedEvent branch retained behind the new ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ gate calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), and the V2 implementation this diff activates under that same flag (ClientPermissionsV2.java:192-195) implements setPermissionsEnabled by throwing UnsupportedOperationException. With the feature enabled, deleting any client fires ClientRemovedEvent into ProviderEventManager.publish, which has no exception handling; when the management() call resolves to the V2 evaluator the UnsupportedOperationException propagates, rolls back the store removal and returns 500 on the delete — the diff's own testManageAllClients delete step sits on exactly this path; even in the best case (V1 routing) the diff ships an evaluator that disavows the cleanup its own listener performs, leaving per-client 'Clients' resources orphaned on every client deletion.

adjudication.rationale: With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled (explicitly checked in AdminPermissions.registerListener), the ClientRemovedEvent handler calls management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). In this diff, MgmtPermissionsV2 overrides clients() to return ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. There is no try/catch in the listener, so if V2 management is used under that feature, client deletion will trigger an exception on the event path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] canExchangeTo is overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException while remaining on the ClientPermissionEvaluator surface whose V1 twin is the token-exchange permission check — this same file's dead getEvaluationContext (lines 258-271) is the verbatim copy of that V1 exchange evaluation context (ClientModelIdentity + kc.client.id attribute). Any token-exchange permission evaluation routed to V2 gets an UnsupportedOperationException instead of a permit/deny decision, so exchanging tokens to a target client fails with a 500 rather than a 403 whenever the V2 evaluator serves that path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that ClientPermissionsV2 overrides token-exchange-related methods (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, and several *Permission methods) to throw UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). It also adds a private getEvaluationContext(...) helper that is not referenced anywhere in ClientPermissionsV2 (apparent dead code) and resembles a token-exchange evaluation context. However, the finding’s stronger claim (that token exchange permission evaluation is routed to V2 and will therefore cause a 500 instead of a 403) cannot be verified from this diff alone because no call sites/routing logic are shown here, and the class explicitly declares the functionality unsupported.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getEvaluationContext is dead code — a private method with no call sites (its only conceivable consumer canExchangeTo throws), sitting alongside the never-used logger field (line 51) and the unused static import AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE (line 46). [ADVISORY] The all-clients fallback inside hasPermission(ClientModel, String) invokes the get-or-create getResourceTypeResource from within a boolean permission check, and AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource is not synchronized, so the first canView/canManage on any client persists a new 'Clients' resource row from a read path. Client list/view endpoints perform resource-store writes during permission evaluation, and two concurrent first evaluations both miss findByName and create duplicate 'Clients' type resources, after which the findByName lookup in hasPermission(String) (line 244) resolves an arbitrary duplicate so all-clients permissions silently stop applying.

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2#hasPermission(ClientModel,String)`, the fallback path when the per-client resource is missing calls `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` from inside a boolean permission check (i.e., on read/evaluation paths like `canView`/`canManage`). From the diff we can verify this call site and that it’s new behavior tied to the new `CLIENTS` resource type, but the finding’s stronger claims (that `getResourceTypeResource` definitely persists a new resource row, that `getOrCreateResource` is used under the hood, that duplicates can be created concurrently, and that `findByName` will later pick an arbitrary duplicate and break all-clients permissions) cannot be proven from this diff because the implementation/constraints of `getResourceTypeResource`, `findByName`, and storage uniqueness are not shown. Still, performing potential create-or-load work from a permission check is a concrete, diff-grounded design concern worth flagging.

Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE), ...)`) and never grant `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` nor exercise an operation that would be gated by it. With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled, deleting any client either dispatches to ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled and aborts the whole client-removal operation with UnsupportedOperationException propagated through the event publish (500/rollback on every client delete), or the listener resolves to the legacy evaluator whose cleanup only touches the legacy resource store while V2 per-client resources (created by AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveClient/getOrCreateResource under the admin-permissions resource server) and their attached scope permissions are never deleted — stale resources accumulate unboundedly and getClientsWithPermission re-evaluates every one of them on each client listing by a non-admin-role user. This diff also introduces MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returning ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2 overrides setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) to throw UnsupportedOperationException (along with other permission-management methods). From the diff alone, if management(...) resolves to MgmtPermissionsV2 under this feature (which is strongly implied by the new V2 classes and the feature-gating of the listener), deleting a client will trigger UnsupportedOperationException during event handling, potentially aborting client deletion. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] canExchangeTo and exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException('Not supported in V2') while remaining on the retained ClientPermissionEvaluator interface, and the new Clients resource type defines no token-exchange scope, so the V1 fine-grained token-exchange capability is silently dropped with no replacement, no documented limitation, and no verification. The diff adds no test asserting the V2 behavior of canExchangeTo (the fully-shown PermissionClientTest contains no exchange test), and the same pattern covers isPermissionsEnabled (187-190), resource (197-200) and getPermissions (202-204); any consumer of the public evaluator interface that runs under the feature-enabled V2 wiring — including existing token-exchange permission checks and the per-client permission-management REST surface — receives an unhandled UnsupportedOperationException (500) instead of a permission decision, and admins in V2 realms cannot configure or query these permissions at all.

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably introduces a V2 implementation (`ClientPermissionsV2`) that is wired in via `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` and that overrides several evaluator methods to throw `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (e.g., `canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`, and multiple `*Permission(...)` methods). The new `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS` resource type also omits any `token-exchange` scope (its scopes are `CONFIGURE, MANAGE, MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, VIEW`). However, from this diff alone we cannot confirm that any runtime code path in the feature-enabled V2 setup actually calls these unsupported methods (and thus would produce 500s), nor can we confirm the intended V2 feature set. What is clear and actionable is that V2 leaves parts of the existing public evaluator surface unimplemented/exception-throwing and adds no tests covering those methods’ V2 behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope and its canMapClientScopeRoles override are shipped with zero test coverage: the complete PermissionClientTest rewrite (all hunks shown before the diff moves to PermissionRESTTest) grants and asserts MANAGE, CONFIGURE, VIEW, MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, but MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE appears in no test and is absent from the test file's static imports (lines 22-27 of the diff). A regression in this override — e.g. a copy-paste of canMapCompositeRoles' scope constant, which sits directly above it — ships undetected, and the client-scope role-mapping operations gated by canMapClientScopeRoles will 403 for admins who were legitimately granted map-roles-client-scope (or, in the inverse direction, over-grant); testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient grants Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE) and thereby proves the sibling scopes work while leaving this one unexercised.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new client scope constant `AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` and wires it into the `CLIENTS` resource type scopes, plus a new `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)` override that checks `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)`. In the updated/expanded `PermissionClientTest`, static imports include `CONFIGURE`, `MANAGE`, `MAP_ROLES`, `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE`, and `VIEW`, but not `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`, and the granted scopes in `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` are `Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE)`—so no test in the shown diff exercises `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` or the `canMapClientScopeRoles` path. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) evaluates only the per-client resource whenever one exists and never consults the type-level 'all clients' grant, contradicting the diff's own javadoc on canManage/canConfigure/canView ('For V2 only: Also if the caller has a permission to ... MANAGE all clients') and creating an asymmetry with canView(client), which short-circuits on the type-level canView() check before the per-client lookup. An admin who grants a user MANAGE on all clients and later creates any per-client Clients permission for client X (even granting a different scope or a different user) silently revokes that user's type-level MANAGE/CONFIGURE/MAP_ROLES grants on X — view still works via the canView() short-circuit but manage stops — and no test in the diff creates both a type-level and a per-client Clients permission to pin the intended precedence, so integrators following the added javadoc will compose grants that silently deny.

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2#hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, if a per-client `Resource` exists (`resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())`), the code evaluates permissions only against that resource and never falls back to the type-level `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` ("all-clients") resource. The type-level resource is consulted only when the per-client resource is `null`. This contradicts the updated interface javadocs for `canManage(ClientModel)`, `canConfigure(ClientModel)`, and mapping methods which state that V2 should also honor type-level grants (e.g., MANAGE/CONFIGURE for all clients). It also creates the asymmetry noted: `canView(ClientModel)` can succeed via `canView()` (which checks type-level `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)`), while `canManage(ClientModel)`/`canConfigure(ClientModel)` can be denied when any per-client resource exists without the needed scope—even if the caller has the type-level grant. The added tests do not cover coexistence of type-level and per-client permissions to define precedence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] resolveClient's two-step resolution (internal id first, then human-readable clientId fallback) and its null path are completely unverified: no test in the diff creates a Clients permission using a client's clientId string, and none covers a nonexistent or foreign-realm client id where resolveClient returns null and getOrCreateResource falls into its name == null branch. The acceptance criterion for the fallback lookup the diff adds is missing — an admin creating a permission with the clientId instead of the internal UUID (the natural thing to copy from the console) gets an untested resolution path; likewise a typo'd or deleted client id reaches the untested name==null branch of getOrCreateResource and yields either a silently-created permission that can never match any client (201 for garbage input) or an unhandled server error, instead of a validated 4xx.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new Clients resource type and a new resolution path in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource(...)` (`else if (CLIENTS.getType().equals(resourceType)) { name = resolveClient(session, id); }`) with `resolveClient` doing a two-step lookup (`getClientById` then `getClientByClientId`) and potentially returning null. The newly added tests in `PermissionClientTest` create client permissions using `myclient.getId()` (internal UUID), not the human-readable `clientId`, and there is no test covering a nonexistent/typo/foreign-realm id that would make `resolveClient` return null and exercise the `name == null` branch in `getOrCreateResource`. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded missing-coverage issue for the new fallback/edge-paths, but the diff alone doesn’t prove a functional defect (what happens on `name == null` isn’t shown).
