[ADVISORY] The three near-identical permission-scan loops (hasPermission(ClientModel,String) at ~206, hasPermission(String) at ~237, hasGrantedPermission at ~277) are copy-pasted with already-observed drift: the realmResourceServer() null-check exists in the first two but not in hasGrantedPermission, and the policyStore.findByResource(...).isEmpty() type-resource guard exists only in the per-client variant. The next change to grant matching — adding a second expected scope, decision caching, or a scope-name variant — must be replicated in three hand-maintained places, and the existing drift shows the copies have already diverged (hasGrantedPermission re-fetches root.realmResourceServer() and dereferences it unguarded, surviving only because its single caller checks first); extracting one shared evaluate(resource, scope) helper deletes the drift and two of the three copies.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2` there are three very similar permission-evaluation loops: `hasPermission(ClientModel,String)`, `hasPermission(String)`, and `hasGrantedPermission(Resource,String)`. They already show drift: `hasGrantedPermission` re-fetches `root.realmResourceServer()` and dereferences it without a null-check, while the other two helpers guard `server == null` (even though the current sole caller `getClientsWithPermission` checks for null before invoking it). Also, the per-client variant has an extra guard `policyStore.findByResource(...).isEmpty()` when falling back to the type resource, which the other helpers don’t mirror. This is a concrete maintainability/consistency issue introduced by the diff and would be better handled by extracting a shared helper.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The PR gates the global role/client/group permission-cleanup listener behind Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ — an unrelated behavioral change smuggled into a PR whose stated intent is only adding a Client resource type and scopes to the authorization schema. Realms that created fine-grained permissions while the feature was enabled and later run with the feature disabled (profile change, config rollback, upgrade drift) silently stop cleaning authorization resource servers on role/client/group deletion; the stale permission data resurrects as live grants over deleted entities when the feature is re-enabled, and the semantic change hides inside a hunk that reindents every line so whitespace-insensitive review tooling shows no gate at all.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in AdminPermissions.registerListener wraps all deletion-event handling (RoleRemovedEvent, ClientRemovedEvent, GroupRemovedEvent) inside `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }`, whereas previously cleanup ran unconditionally. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral change: when the feature is disabled, the listener will no longer call `setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)` on deletions, so any previously-created fine-grained permission artifacts would not be cleaned up during that period. The claim about “reindents every line” is also supported by the hunk showing widespread whitespace/formatting changes alongside the new gate, which can reduce review visibility. However, the more severe claim about stale data “resurrecting as live grants” on re-enable is plausible but not directly provable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The PR introduces persisted per-client Clients-typed authorization resources (read via resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId())) but ships no cleanup when a client is deleted — the designated hook, the ClientRemovedEvent listener's clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client,false), dispatches either to this V2 override that unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException or to the V1 implementation that only deletes per-client resource servers the V2 model never creates, so orphans are never removed in either dispatch. Every client deleted in an FGAP-enabled realm leaves an orphaned resource plus its scope permissions in the realm resource server; the orphans surface as ghost entries in the authz admin API and console and are re-scanned and policy-evaluated by getClientsWithPermission on every filtered client list, accumulating without bound.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds V2 client resource-type support that relies on persisted per-client authorization resources named by `client.getId()` (`ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String)` does `resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())`, and `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` can create CLIENTS-typed resources via `resolveClient`). However, the existing cleanup hook on deletion (`AdminPermissions.registerListener`: on `ClientRemovedEvent` it calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)`) will invoke `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` when V2 is used, and that returns `ClientPermissionsV2` where `setPermissionsEnabled` unconditionally throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. So, in V2 mode, client deletion will not clean up and will likely fail at runtime during event handling; regardless, no V2 cleanup implementation is present in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ClientPermissionsV2 replaces the entire V1 permission-management surface (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, the mapRoles*/managePermission/configurePermission/viewPermission Policy getters, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) with unconditional throw new UnsupportedOperationException instead of a designed de-scoping response, while the admin REST endpoints these evaluator methods back remain live. Administrators on FGAP-enabled realms using the existing client management/permissions endpoints (legacy console, provisioning scripts) and any token-exchange flow that consults canExchangeTo receive raw 500 Internal Server Errors rather than a controlled 4xx or feature-gated response.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` is overridden to return `ClientPermissionsV2` (services/.../MgmtPermissionsV2.java). `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides multiple methods including `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel client, boolean enable)` and makes them unconditionally `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (services/.../ClientPermissionsV2.java). Meanwhile, the admin permission cleanup listener still calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` on `ClientRemovedEvent` when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). If the V2 permissions implementation is in use under that feature (as the class naming/override suggests), this creates a directly-triggerable runtime exception path (client removal) that would surface as an internal error rather than a controlled response/behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles evaluate only explicit map-roles grants and drop the MANAGE_CLIENTS coarse-role fallback that the same class's canManage(client), canManageClientScopes and canView overrides all retain, so an administrator holding the manage-clients role is denied client role mapping in V2 realms. Realm administrators with the manage-clients role get 403 on client role-assignment and composite-role endpoints that gate on these evaluators — a silent reversal of V1 semantics where manage-clients sufficed — and no test in the diff exercises the coarse-role path through these methods, so the narrowing ships unverified.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, ClientPermissionsV2.canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles intentionally return only hasPermission(..., MAP_ROLES*), with no AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS fallback. The updated interface Javadocs for these methods also describe only permission-based checks (including “all clients” permissions for V2) and do not state that MANAGE_CLIENTS should grant these mapping abilities. Therefore, the finding’s core assertion—"manage-clients coarse-role should suffice and is now wrongly denied"—is not verifiable from the diff and contradicts the documented intent shown here. While tests indeed don’t cover a MANAGE_CLIENTS-path, the diff doesn’t establish that such a path is required for these methods.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getEvaluationContext is dead code — no method in ClientPermissionsV2 calls it because the token-exchange methods it was written to support were stubbed to throw — and the TOKEN_EXCHANGE static import (line 44), the never-used Logger field (line 49), and the ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext imports exist only to serve this abandoned half-implementation. The next maintainer of the exchange-permission path must reverse-engineer whether token-exchange support was meant to ship, or wires the dead scaffolding in believing it is live; dead security-adjacent code in a permission evaluator also misleads audits of the effective permission surface.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2` class, `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` is not referenced anywhere in that file, while the token-exchange related methods it would likely support (`canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, etc.) are overridden to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. Additionally, `private static final Logger logger = ...` is declared but never used, and the static import `AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE` is present but not used anywhere in the class. This is diff-grounded dead/scaffolding code that can mislead future maintenance/audits, but it does not by itself demonstrate a functional defect in the shown behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff contradicts itself on who can enumerate clients: the canList/requireList javadoc added here defines listing as canView() or QUERY_CLIENTS/QUERY_USERS (and the shipped evaluator returns false for a caller holding only a type-level MANAGE grant), yet testManageAllClients in the same diff asserts that exact caller lists all clients — behavior nothing in this diff provides. Either the added test is red, or the client-listing endpoint bypasses the documented canList contract, leaving an undocumented widening of client enumeration; a maintainer implementing or auditing the list endpoint against this javadoc enforces the wrong set of list-capable principals on a security boundary.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce an internal inconsistency between the newly added/expanded javadocs on client enumeration and what the new tests expect. In `ClientPermissionEvaluator`, `canList()` is documented as true if `canView()` is true or the caller has `QUERY_CLIENTS`/`QUERY_USERS` roles (no mention of MANAGE). Yet `PermissionClientTest#testManageAllClients` grants only a type-level `MANAGE` permission via `createAllPermission(..., Set.of(MANAGE))` and then asserts `realmAdminClient.realm(...).clients().findAll()` returns a non-empty list. The diff does not show the list endpoint implementation nor the inherited `canList()` logic (ClientPermissionsV2 does not override `canList()`), so we cannot prove the test is red or the endpoint bypasses `canList()`. What is verifiable from the diff is that the documentation and tests describe different expectations for who can enumerate clients, which is a security-sensitive contract/documentation issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Three hand-maintained copies of the 'granted permissions carry scope X' loop exist (hasPermission(ClientModel,String) here, hasPermission(String), and hasGrantedPermission) and already show textual drift — two match via Arrays.asList(scope).contains(s), the third via scope.equals(s). The next change to scope matching (name normalization, case handling) applied to one copy silently diverges grant decisions between the per-client, all-clients and list-filter paths; a single hasScope(Collection<Permission>, String) helper deletes ~12 lines and the drift site.

adjudication.rationale: In new `ClientPermissionsV2`, there are three separate, hand-written loops that test whether an evaluated `Collection<Permission>` contains a given scope: `hasPermission(ClientModel,String)` and `hasPermission(String)` both build `List<String> expectedScopes = Arrays.asList(scope)` and then check `expectedScopes.contains(s)`, while `hasGrantedPermission(Resource,String)` checks `scope.equals(s)`. This is diff-verifiable textual drift and creates a concrete maintenance risk: if scope matching logic is later changed (normalization/case/etc.) and only one copy is updated, the per-client check, all-clients check, and list-filter path can diverge. A small shared helper (e.g., `hasScope(permissions, scope)`) would eliminate the duplicated drift point.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] canManageClientScopes, canManage(ClientScopeModel) and canView(ClientScopeModel) evaluate the Clients-typed all-clients resource, so a permission whose resource type is 'Clients' silently governs realm client-scope entities — a distinct entity kind that has no resource type in this schema. An operator applying least privilege by granting manage on all clients unknowingly grants create/delete over realm client scopes, whose defaults are inherited by every client in the realm — the grant's reach exceeds what its named resource type advertises, and the schema enforces no invariant tying a permission to the entity kind it governs.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows ClientPermissionsV2 authorizes realm ClientScopeModel operations via the Clients resource type: canManageClientScopes() returns hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), canManage(ClientScopeModel) delegates to canManageClientScopes(), and canView(ClientScopeModel) checks hasPermission(VIEW) || hasPermission(MANAGE). The underlying hasPermission(String) evaluates a resource named AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE ("Clients") (i.e., the all-clients resource), and AdminPermissionsSchema adds no distinct resource type for client scopes. So a permission on the Clients-typed resource can govern client-scope entities without an explicit schema invariant tying the permission’s resource type to that entity kind. Whether intended or not, this is a concrete authorization-model coupling introduced/relied upon by the diff and is a legitimate least-privilege/semantics concern, though not provably a functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The by-clientId fallback branch of resolveClient (getClientByClientId) is exercised by no test in this diff — every visible test passes internal IDs — so the normalization contract that the resource be named by the internal ID (matching ClientPermissionsV2's findByName(server, client.getId()) lookup) ships unverified. A regression in resolveClient that returns the raw clientId as the resource name silently denies every per-client grant (hasPermission falls through to the all-clients type resource and returns false), and no test in the suite fails to catch it.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveClient() adds a fallback lookup via getClientByClientId(realm, id) but returns client.getId() either way. However, the new/modified tests (e.g., PermissionClientTest) create per-client permissions using internal IDs (myclient.getId(), realmClient.getId()), so only the getClientById path is exercised. No test passes a clientId string into permission creation to validate that the fallback branch still normalizes the resource name to the internal ID, which ClientPermissionsV2 later assumes via resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()). This is a concrete missing-test gap for newly added logic, not a demonstrated defect in the current implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope and its evaluator entry point canMapClientScopeRoles ship with zero coverage — no visible test in the diff grants or asserts that scope anywhere. The map-roles-client-scope capability ships unverifiable: a typo or mis-wiring in the scope name silently denies (or over-grants) client-scope role mapping with no failing test, leaving the scope as inert surface until an operator discovers it does nothing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces the new scope constant `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` in `AdminPermissionsSchema` and wires an evaluator entry point `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles()` that checks `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)`. However, the added/modified tests in `PermissionClientTest` only grant/assert scopes like `MANAGE`, `CONFIGURE`, `VIEW`, `MAP_ROLES`, and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` (e.g., `createPermission(... Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE) ...)`) and never grant or assert `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`. So the finding about zero visible test coverage for this newly added scope is grounded in the diff and is a concrete review issue (coverage gap), not a directly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles and canMapClientScopeRoles are permission-only overrides that drop the AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS role short-circuit that every other method in this same class retains (canManage(client) line 66, canManageClientScopes line 107, canView via canViewClientDefault), breaking the V2 formula of 'static role OR fine-grained permission' for exactly these three checks. In any realm running the V2 evaluator, an admin holding the static manage-clients role (including full realm-admin) gets 403 from requireMapRoles when mapping that client's roles to a user, adding composite roles, or adding client-scope roles — operations V1 granted to manage-clients holders; the new tests only exercise the fine-granted 'myadmin' user and never a manage-clients admin, so the suite cannot catch it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that ClientPermissionsV2.canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles only call hasPermission(...) and do not short-circuit on AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS, unlike canManage/canManageClientScopes/canView. However, the same PR also updates the ClientPermissionEvaluator Javadoc for these map-roles methods to describe them as permission-based checks only (no mention of MANAGE_CLIENTS), while other methods explicitly document the MANAGE_CLIENTS/VIEW_CLIENTS role short-circuits. The finding’s claim that this "breaks the V2 formula" and causes 403s for manage-clients/realm-admin cannot be verified from the diff (requireMapRoles behavior and any realm-admin bypass/default policies are not shown), and it contradicts the diff’s stated contract for these methods.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The removal-cleanup listener is guarded by Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) while the evaluator returned by management() is the V2 subclass selected by the separate V2 feature switch, so in a deployment with both features enabled the guard passes and line 92 calls MgmtPermissionsV2.clients().setPermissionsEnabled, whose ClientPermissionsV2 override throws UnsupportedOperationException. With both feature flags on, DELETE /admin/realms/{r}/clients/{id} fires ClientRemovedEvent into the synchronous listener, the V2 stub throws, the exception propagates out of the event publish, and every client removal in the realm fails with a 500; the test suite passes only because its config keeps ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ off.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a concrete inconsistency: the listener in AdminPermissions.registerListener() is now guarded only by Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and on ClientRemovedEvent it calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(..., false), while the new V2 implementation MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2 whose setPermissionsEnabled() unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. However, the diff does not show how management(...) selects MgmtPermissionsV2 vs the non-V2 implementation, nor whether that selection is tied to a separate feature flag as the finding claims. So the exact “both flags enabled => client deletion always 500” behavior cannot be fully verified from the provided diff alone, though the risk is real if ClientPermissionsV2 can be returned under the listener guard.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getClientsWithPermission runs a full policy evaluation per resource inside the resourceStore.findByType callback (hasGrantedPermission → root.evaluatePermission at lines 274-276), an N+1 evaluation loop over every Clients-type resource with no batching, caching, or limit. The client-list flow that filters by per-client permissions (the diff's own tests show findAll() returning only permitted clients) performs one complete authorization-engine evaluation — each resolving and running its policy set against the user/role stores — per permission-bearing client resource in the realm; a realm with hundreds of per-client permissions turns every admin Clients-page load into hundreds of sequential evaluations, the exact profile that got the V1 feature disabled by default for performance.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission(String)` method, the code iterates all resources of type `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` via `resourceStore.findByType(...)` and, inside the callback, calls `hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope)`. `hasGrantedPermission` performs a full `root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(...))` for each resource, i.e., one authorization-engine evaluation per client resource. This is an N-per-resource evaluation pattern (no batching/caching/short-circuit beyond scope match) that can become costly in realms with many client resources/permissions. It’s a performance/architecture concern grounded in the diff, not a functional correctness defect proven by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] canExchangeTo is overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException while remaining on the shared ClientPermissionEvaluator surface that the token-exchange flow invokes, and the new Clients resource type (AdminPermissionsSchema line 67) omits any token-exchange scope, so V1's per-client token-exchange grant has no representation in the V2 schema at all. Client-to-client token exchange in a realm where the fine-grained exchange check is active hits the throwing stub and surfaces a raw 500 instead of a grant/deny decision; wherever the check is instead skipped, the V1 policy restriction on exchange silently disappears so any client may exchange — the operator gets either a crash or an unguarded bypass with no policy-governed middle.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that V2 client permissions intentionally do not support token-exchange: `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides `canExchangeTo(...)` and multiple permission-creation methods to throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (new file, several overrides), and the new `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS` resource type scopes list omits any token-exchange-related scope (only CONFIGURE/MANAGE/MAP_ROLES*/VIEW). However, the finding’s stronger claim that the token-exchange flow will invoke these methods and therefore cause a raw 500 or a bypass cannot be verified from this diff alone because no token-exchange call sites or feature wiring are included here. What is verifiable is a parity/coverage gap for token-exchange in the V2 schema/evaluator surface.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Eleven working V1 methods (exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, mapRolesCompositePermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) are replaced by raw UnsupportedOperationException throws with no feature gate, HTTP status mapping, or replacement path on the shared evaluator interface. The existing admin API surface that manages per-client fine-grained permissions — e.g. the client management-permissions toggle endpoints (GET/PUT /clients/{id}/management-permissions, which call isPermissionsEnabled/getPermissions/setPermissionsEnabled) — turns from working responses into unhandled 500s the moment the V2 evaluator is active; operators and the admin console get server errors instead of a 4xx 'not supported in V2'.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ClientPermissionsV2 extends ClientPermissions` and overrides the listed methods (`exchangeToPermission`, `mapRolesPermission`, `mapRolesClientScopePermission`, `mapRolesCompositePermission`, `managePermission`, `configurePermission`, `viewPermission`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`, plus `canExchangeTo`) to unconditionally `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. There is no feature-gate or alternative behavior shown around these throws in this class, and `MgmtPermissionsV2#clients()` now returns this V2 implementation. However, the diff does not show the REST endpoints or call sites that would invoke these methods (e.g., management-permissions toggle endpoints), so the claim that they definitively become unhandled 500s cannot be fully verified from the diff alone; it is a concrete compatibility/completeness concern created by the change, not a provable regression within the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The diff introduces per-client permission resources (AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creating Clients-type resources named by client ID) but provides no cleanup when a client is deleted: the only removal hook, the ClientRemovedEvent listener, is feature-gated off in V2 deployments by this same diff, and the V2 setPermissionsEnabled override throws instead of deleting anything. Every client that ever had a fine-grained permission leaves an orphaned Resource plus its scope-permission rows in the admin resource server after deletion; orphans accumulate unboundedly, still surface in the global scope-permission listing the tests iterate, and are re-evaluated on every getClientsWithPermission list request forever.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds per-client authorization Resources under the new CLIENTS resource type (AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS + resolveClient() and getOrCreateResource() now creating/using resources named by client.getId()). Cleanup on deletion still relies on AdminPermissions.registerListener() calling management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false) for ClientRemovedEvent, but in V2 MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2 where setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) is overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException. The diff does not add any alternative resource/policy deletion path for V2, so client-deletion will not clean up (and may even throw at runtime when the listener runs), leaving stored authz Resources/permissions orphaned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ClientPermissionsV2 carries dead V1 skeleton code: getEvaluationContext (lines 262-272) has no caller since canExchangeTo now throws, the static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE (line 46) is unused, and the logger field (line 51) is never written to. The next maintainer debugging token-exchange authorization reads an apparently-live evaluation-context path that can never execute, and the copied import/field suggest exchange support exists when it does not; deleting the method plus both unused declarations removes ~15 lines with zero behavior change.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2` file, `canExchangeTo(...)` and related exchange/map permission methods all throw `UnsupportedOperationException`, and there is no reference in the diff to the private `getEvaluationContext(...)` helper (it is defined but never called). Additionally, `private static final Logger logger = ...` is declared but unused, and the static import `AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE` is not referenced anywhere in the class. These are diff-grounded maintainability issues (dead/unused code that can mislead), not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The granted-scope matching loop is pasted three times (hasPermission(ClientModel,String) lines 224-232, hasPermission(String) lines 249-257, hasGrantedPermission lines 276-283) and the copies have already drifted: two match via Arrays.asList(scope).contains(s), the third via scope.equals(s). Any future change to how granted scopes are matched (e.g. parameterized scopes or prefix matching) must be applied in three private copies that give no compile error when missed, so the three permission-check paths can silently disagree on what counts as granted.

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2` there are three separate loops that inspect `Permission.getScopes()` (`hasPermission(ClientModel,String)`, `hasPermission(String)`, and `hasGrantedPermission`). Two use `Arrays.asList(scope).contains(s)` while the third uses `scope.equals(s)`. Although these are equivalent for a single scope value (so it’s not a verifiable bug from the diff), the duplicated matching logic is real and creates maintainability risk: any future change to scope-matching semantics would need to be applied in multiple places and could diverge without compiler help.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException while this same diff's AdminPermissions ClientRemovedEvent handler (AdminPermissions.java lines 89-91, also in this diff) calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), so the PR ships no configuration in which deleting a client removes its permission resources. In any deployment where AdminPermissions.management() resolves to MgmtPermissionsV2 while the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ gate on the listener passes, deleting any client throws UnsupportedOperationException during event dispatch and the delete fails/rolls back (the V1 contract that ClientRemovedEvent cleans up client permissions is destroyed); where the gate keeps the listener dormant, the per-client 'Clients' resource created via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource is silently orphaned, so getClientsWithPermission iterates stale resources and the authorization store accumulates garbage with no removal path.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, AdminPermissions.registerListener() (services/.../AdminPermissions.java) handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled and calls management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). Meanwhile, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() is overridden to return ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException ("Not supported in V2"). Therefore, in any runtime configuration where management(...) returns a MgmtPermissionsV2 instance while the listener gate passes, client deletion will trigger an UnsupportedOperationException during event dispatch instead of cleaning up/turning off permissions, breaking expected behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] canExchangeTo and exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException, deleting the token-exchange permission path that V1 serves, while the new Clients resource type omits the token-exchange scope so no V2 grant can ever replace it. With the V2 admin permissions feature active, the client-to-client token-exchange permission check throws an unhandled exception (500 on the token endpoint) instead of evaluating or denying; a realm moving from V1 fine-grained permissions loses documented, working token-exchange behavior with no scope in the new schema to re-grant it and no accepted alternative in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces a V2 client-permissions implementation where token-exchange related APIs are explicitly unsupported: `ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo(...)` and `exchangeToPermission(...)` (and related permission builders) unconditionally `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. Additionally, the new `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS` resource type scopes (`CONFIGURE`, `MANAGE`, `MAP_ROLES`, `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`, `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE`, `VIEW`) omit any token-exchange scope. This is a concrete, diff-grounded feature/parity gap: under `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` the system will use `ClientPermissionsV2`, so any code path that relies on these token-exchange permission methods will not be able to evaluate/deny via V2 and has no schema scope to re-grant token exchange. However, the claim about an unhandled exception causing a 500 on the token endpoint cannot be verified from this diff alone because the token endpoint call sites/exception handling are not shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The whole V1 per-client permission-management surface (managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, mapRolesCompositePermission, isPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, resource) is kept as public API but stubbed to throw, with no feature-gating of the REST/console endpoints that call these methods. Operators who enable the V2 feature and open a client's Permissions tab (or invoke the V1 permission-management REST endpoints) get unhandled 500 responses rather than a feature-appropriate 4xx or a disabled surface, because nothing in the diff turns those endpoints off under V2.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that under V2, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns `ClientPermissionsV2`, and `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides several previously-supported per-client permission-management methods (`managePermission`, `configurePermission`, `viewPermission`, `mapRolesPermission`, `mapRolesClientScopePermission`, `mapRolesCompositePermission`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`, etc.) to unconditionally throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (new file `ClientPermissionsV2.java`). If any existing REST/UI code path calls these methods while V2 is active, it would result in an exception at runtime (potentially a 500). However, the finding’s specific claim that the REST/console endpoints are not feature-gated and will definitely produce unhandled 500s cannot be verified from this diff alone because no endpoint/controller code is shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Dead token-exchange scaffolding is left in the shipped file: the private getEvaluationContext method has no caller once canExchangeTo throws, the static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE (line 46) is unused, and the logger field (line 51) is never read. Maintainers reading the class are misled into believing V2 token-exchange evaluation is implemented or imminent; all three artifacts are deletable with zero behavior change, and the next token-exchange change starts from stale, misleading scaffolding.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2` class, `canExchangeTo(...)` and other token-exchange related methods immediately `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`, and within the diff there is no caller for the private `getEvaluationContext(...)` helper. Also, `import static org.keycloak.services.resources.admin.permissions.AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE;` is present but `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` is never referenced, and `private static final Logger logger = Logger.getLogger(ClientPermissionsV2.class);` is declared but not used. These are diff-verifiable dead/misleading scaffolding artifacts and can be removed without changing behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The permission/scope matching loop is hand-duplicated three times in one new class (hasPermission(ClientModel,String) lines 225-233, hasPermission(String) lines 250-258, hasGrantedPermission lines 277-284) and the copies have already diverged in style (Arrays.asList(scope).contains(s) vs scope.equals(s)). Any future change to scope-matching semantics (e.g., matching a scope set or normalizing scope names) must be applied in three places; missing one yields inconsistent permission decisions between canManage/canView/canMapRoles and getClientsWithPermission for the same grant, with no test forced to catch the divergence.

adjudication.rationale: In the new class `ClientPermissionsV2`, the scope-grant check logic is indeed hand-duplicated in three methods: `hasPermission(ClientModel,String)` (loops over `Permission`/scopes and checks `expectedScopes.contains(s)`), `hasPermission(String)` (same pattern), and `hasGrantedPermission(Resource,String)` (same loop but uses `scope.equals(s)`). This is diff-grounded duplication that can lead to inconsistent behavior if scope-matching semantics change later, even though it is not a current, verifiable functional defect in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] canMapClientScopeRoles (the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope this diff adds to the Clients schema) is the only new Clients scope with no test anywhere in the diff, while every sibling scope (MANAGE, CONFIGURE, VIEW, MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE) gets end-to-end assertions in PermissionClientTest. A regression in the scope constant or in the wiring of canMapClientScopeRoles to the client-scope role-mapping endpoints passes CI silently, leaving admins granted map-roles-client-scope with a silent no-op (or an over-grant) on those endpoints.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new Clients scope constant `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` in `AdminPermissionsSchema` and wires it via `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)` to `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)`. However, the updated/added end-to-end tests in `PermissionClientTest` assert behavior for `MANAGE`, `CONFIGURE`, `VIEW`, `MAP_ROLES`, and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` (e.g., `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient`), but there is no test that grants `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` and exercises the client-scope role-mapping endpoints. This creates a concrete gap where a regression in the constant or authorization wiring for `canMapClientScopeRoles` could pass CI unnoticed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, and the ClientRemovedEvent handler this same diff wires up (AdminPermissions.java:91 calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) under the new Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) gate) invokes it for every client deleted while the feature is enabled — the exact state in which MgmtPermissionsV2 serves clients() with this V2 evaluator. With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled, deleting any client throws UnsupportedOperationException from the event listener: DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id} returns 500 and the removal rolls back (leaving the client undeletable) or leaves dangling V2 authorization resources, and the diff's own testManageAllClients delete step cannot succeed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a ClientRemovedEvent handler under the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature gate that always calls `management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)` (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). In the same diff, the V2 client permission evaluator `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel client, boolean enable)` to unconditionally throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (services/.../ClientPermissionsV2.java). Also in this diff, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` is overridden to return `new ClientPermissionsV2(...)` (services/.../MgmtPermissionsV2.java). Therefore, when the feature is enabled and the management layer uses `MgmtPermissionsV2`, deleting a client will trigger the listener and can throw `UnsupportedOperationException` during client removal, causing a 500/error path instead of clean cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] canExchangeTo unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException while the method remains on the retained ClientPermissionEvaluator surface whose V1 token-exchange authorization path (the runtime check that a client may exchange a token into a target client, evidenced by the copied-but-unused getEvaluationContext helper at line 246) still calls it whenever V2 is the active evaluator. In realms with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (and token-exchange) enabled, a cross-client token exchange that previously evaluated the token-exchange permission now crashes with a 500 on the protocol endpoint instead of returning a grant/deny decision.

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably introduces `ClientPermissionsV2` where `canExchangeTo(...)` (and related token-exchange permission methods) unconditionally throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (see `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides). If any runtime path selects the V2 evaluator (`MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns `ClientPermissionsV2`) and still invokes these methods, that would result in a 500 rather than an authorization decision. However, the diff does not show the token-exchange call sites or feature gating for these methods, so the claim that the “V1 token-exchange authorization path still calls it whenever V2 is active” cannot be confirmed from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getClientsWithPermission runs a full policy evaluation (hasGrantedPermission → root.evaluatePermission, each hitting the policy store) for every Clients-type resource on each call, making the client-list filtering path cost O(number of permission-bearing clients) evaluations per HTTP request. An admin holding per-client grants in a realm where hundreds of clients carry fine-grained permissions pays hundreds of policy evaluations on every admin-console client list, so list latency grows linearly with the number of permissioned clients — the feature's primary use case.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission(String), the code iterates over every resource of type AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE via resourceStore.findByType(...). For each resource it calls hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope), which performs root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server), server). This is a full permission evaluation per resource, so the runtime cost is proportional to the number of client resources scanned, matching the O(N) per-request evaluation concern described. This is a diff-grounded performance/scalability issue rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The deny path of hasPermission(ClientModel, String) mutates persistent state: when the per-client resource is absent it calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource (get-or-create), so a permission check — including one that ends in deny — creates the 'Clients' type resource in the authorization store. Operators see authorization-store rows written by read-only admin operations (e.g., an ungranted admin's first GET on any client in a fresh realm triggers the creation), so permission evaluation is not side-effect-free and any read-only or replicated evaluation context is broken by a write during a check.

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when `resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())` returns null, the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` before checking whether any policies exist (`policyStore.findByResource(...)`). Given the method name and pattern used elsewhere in `AdminPermissionsSchema` (e.g., `getOrCreateResource`), this fallback is plausibly a get-or-create that may persist the "Clients" type resource even when the permission check ultimately returns false. The diff doesn’t show `getResourceTypeResource`’s implementation, so the persistent-write claim can’t be proven here, but the new call site during permission evaluation is real and could introduce side effects.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The ClientRemovedEvent branch calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false), which this same PR wires to ClientPermissionsV2 (via MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()) whose setPermissionsEnabled override throws UnsupportedOperationException, so client-removal permission cleanup cannot execute in exactly the configuration (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled, V2 active) that every test in this diff runs under. Deleting any client with fine-grained permissions under V2 either throws inside the event listener (failing DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id} with a 500 if the exception propagates) or, if the event dispatch swallows it, silently orphans the client's authorization resource; testManageAllClients only removes 'newClient', a client with no permission resource, so no test in the diff removes a permissioned client and the broken cleanup path ships undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows AdminPermissions.registerListener() calling management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false) on ClientRemovedEvent (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). This PR also wires MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() to return ClientPermissionsV2 (services/.../MgmtPermissionsV2.java), and ClientPermissionsV2 overrides setPermissionsEnabled(...) to unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException (services/.../ClientPermissionsV2.java). Therefore, in any runtime where management(...) resolves to MgmtPermissionsV2, the client-removal cleanup path will throw at event time, breaking or skipping permission cleanup for deleted clients.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient grants MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE and CONFIGURE in a single permission before asserting the role-mapping operations succeed, so the assertions cannot attribute authorization to any specific scope — if canMapCompositeRoles in ClientPermissionsV2 checked MAP_ROLES or CONFIGURE instead of MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, this test still passes. A scope-constant swap in the three near-identical V2 overrides (canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles) ships with a green suite: the discriminating case — grant MAP_ROLES only and assert addComposites still returns 403 — is absent, so composite-role administration gets wrongly granted or wrongly denied in production with no CI signal.

adjudication.rationale: In PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient, the permission created for the client resource grants multiple scopes at once: Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE). The subsequent success assertions (adding client-level role to a user, and addComposites) therefore do not isolate which specific scope is required for which operation. Given the three near-identical ClientPermissionsV2 overrides (canMapRoles -> MAP_ROLES, canMapCompositeRoles -> MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, canMapClientScopeRoles -> MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE), this test would not catch an accidental constant swap/mis-check in canMapCompositeRoles because MAP_ROLES/CONFIGURE are also granted in the same permission. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap, not a verifiable functional defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope and the canMapClientScopeRoles override are covered by no test in the diff's test changes (checked: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/AbstractPermissionTest.java, PermissionClientTest.java, PermissionRESTTest.java, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java — PermissionClientTest's imported scopes are exactly CONFIGURE, MANAGE, MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, VIEW, and no test grants MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE or calls a client scope-mapping endpoint). A copy-paste error in this one-liner sibling of canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles — the likeliest regression in this exact trio of new scopes — makes the admin client scope-mapping endpoints (POST /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/scope-mappings) grant or deny the wrong principals with no failing test.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new client scope `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` (AdminPermissionsSchema) and adds V2 authorization logic for it via `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel client)` which delegates to `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)`. In the shown test changes, `PermissionClientTest` only grants/uses scopes `CONFIGURE`, `MANAGE`, `MAP_ROLES`, `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE`, and `VIEW` (and never `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`), and no added/modified test exercises a client scope-mapping path that would depend on `canMapClientScopeRoles`. So the specific new permission path is not covered by tests in this diff. The finding’s “copy-paste error is likely” part is speculative and not verifiable from the diff, but the missing test coverage for this new scope/logic is concrete and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The admin-role fast paths of the new V2 evaluator — canManage(ClientModel)'s root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS), canManage()'s super.canManage(), and canView()'s canViewClientDefault() — are exercised by no test in the diff, because every visible test authenticates as 'myadmin', a user with no admin roles who is granted only type/resource permissions. A regression that breaks the MANAGE_CLIENTS/VIEW_CLIENTS role bypass under V2 keeps the entire suite green while locking realm administrators out of all client management on any realm with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled; only the role-less permission path is verified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces ClientPermissionsV2 role-based short-circuit paths (e.g., canManage(ClientModel) returns true when root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS); canManage() delegates to super.canManage(); canView() delegates to canViewClientDefault()). The newly added/modified tests in PermissionClientTest and related classes consistently authenticate as the managed user "myadmin" and explicitly assert operations are Forbidden until fine-grained scope permissions are created (e.g., testManageOnlyOneClient/testManageAllClients/testViewAllClients), which implies "myadmin" is not relying on MANAGE_CLIENTS/VIEW_CLIENTS fast-path roles in these scenarios. No test in the diff demonstrates that an admin-role-bearing caller is allowed via these bypasses under V2, so a regression in the admin-role checks could go undetected while permission-based tests stay green.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new resolveClient fallback branch (session.clients().getClientByClientId(realm, id), lines 179-181) is never tested — every test in the diff addresses client permissions by internal id (myclient.getId()), while the analogous username fallback for USERS is covered by PermissionRESTTest.resourcesTest, and no test creates a client permission addressed by clientId. If the fallback or the new CLIENTS branch in getOrCreateResource (lines 92-93) regresses, creating a client permission by clientId resolves a null name and the request fails for any caller that addresses clients by clientId (the natural analog of the tested username path), and nothing in CI catches it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new CLIENTS resource type plus resolveClient() with a fallback from getClientById(realm,id) to getClientByClientId(realm,id), and wires it into getOrCreateResource() (new CLIENTS branch). In the updated/added tests, client permissions are created either for all clients (no resource id) or for a specific client using the internal UUID (e.g., PermissionClientTest uses myclient.getId() when calling createPermission(..., myclient.getId(), clientsType, ...)). Unlike the USERS path (PermissionRESTTest.resourcesTest creates a permission with resources(Set.of(userAlice.getUsername())) to exercise resolveUser fallback), there is no test that creates a client permission addressed by clientId (e.g., "myclient") to exercise resolveClient’s fallback branch and the new CLIENTS handling in getOrCreateResource. This is a concrete, diff-grounded missing-test gap, not a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The V2 overrides gating realm-level client-scope administration — canManageClientScopes(), canManage(ClientScopeModel) and canView(ClientScopeModel) — are covered by no test in the diff: the visible tests only touch per-client default/optional client-scope endpoints and never the /admin/realms/{realm}/client-scopes CRUD endpoints these methods authorize. A wrong gate on realm client-scope create/update/delete under V2 (e.g., canView(ClientScopeModel) or canManageClientScopes evaluating the wrong scope or role constant) ships undetected, and operators cannot tell from the suite whether client-scope administration is authorized correctly under the new model.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new V2 authorization logic for realm-level client-scope administration in `ClientPermissionsV2`, specifically `canManageClientScopes()`, `canManage(ClientScopeModel)`, and `canView(ClientScopeModel)` (new/overridden in `services/.../ClientPermissionsV2.java`). The new tests added/modified in this diff (notably `PermissionClientTest`) exercise per-client endpoints like `ClientResource#getDefaultClientScopes()`, `removeDefaultClientScope`, `addOptionalClientScope`, secrets, protocol mappers, and client CRUD; they do not exercise realm-level `/admin/realms/{realm}/client-scopes` CRUD flows that would be authorized by the `ClientScopeModel`-based gates. Therefore, a regression in those V2 methods (wrong role/scope checks) would not be caught by the tests shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The false-branch of the newly added Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) guard — skipping the RoleRemoved/ClientRemoved/GroupRemoved permission cleanup entirely — is triggered by no test in the diff, since every test runs on the feature-enabled KeycloakAdminPermissionsServerConfig. Realms where fine-grained permissions were created and the feature was then disabled now silently leak authorization resources on every role/client/group removal (before this gate the cleanup ran unconditionally), and the suite gives no signal about the changed behavior of feature-disabled deployments.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes AdminPermissions.registerListener so that RoleRemoved/ClientRemoved/GroupRemoved cleanup only runs when Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled (new outer `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(...)) { ... }`). Previously, the cleanup ran unconditionally for those events. The finding’s point that the added guard’s disabled-feature path is not exercised by any tests in this diff is supported: the new/modified tests shown are all under the fine-grained authz test suite/config (e.g., `@KeycloakIntegrationTest(config = KeycloakAdminPermissionsServerConfig.class)` in PermissionClientTest) and do not cover feature-disabled behavior. Whether skipping cleanup when the feature is disabled is an actual defect (resource/policy “leak”) can’t be conclusively verified from the diff alone (it may be intended), but the behavior change and missing test coverage for the disabled path are concrete and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The private getEvaluationContext(authorizedClient, token) helper is dead code — no method in the class calls it, since the V1 canExchangeTo that used it is overridden to throw — and the unused logger field (line 51) plus the ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext/EvaluationContext imports, the unused Scope import, and the unused static TOKEN_EXCHANGE import exist only as leftover V1 scaffolding. The next reader of V2 concludes client-identity token-exchange evaluation exists here when it actually throws, and the next change to this class must first disentangle which imports, the logger, and the helper are live; deleting the method plus its now-unused imports and field removes ~15 lines with zero behavioral impact.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) is overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"), yet the ClientRemovedEvent listener retained in this same PR (AdminPermissions.java:92) calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on every client deletion in feature-enabled realms, so the removal-cleanup path throws instead of executing. With the admin permissions feature enabled, deleting any client surfaces UnsupportedOperationException (failing the delete request, or completing with the exception logged post-commit depending on where the event fires), and the deleted client's Clients-type resource and its attached policies are never removed — orphaned rows accumulate in the authorization store and getClientsWithPermission keeps handing out IDs of deleted clients; no test in the diff deletes a client that actually has permission resources, so the one case the cleanup exists for is unexercised.

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener(), when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled the listener handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). In this PR, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() is overridden to return ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2 overrides setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) to throw UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). Therefore, if management(...) resolves to MgmtPermissionsV2 under the same feature flag, a client deletion will trigger an exception during the removal event handling instead of performing cleanup (and the intended disable/cleanup behavior won’t run).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles evaluate only explicit MAP_ROLES/MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE/MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE permissions with no hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS) fallback, unlike canManage/canView/canConfigure in the same class which all include the admin-role bypass. Admins holding the manage-clients realm role are Forbidden from every client role-mapping operation (assigning client roles to users, adding composites, binding client-scope roles) in V2-enabled realms unless someone hand-creates type-level map-roles permissions, because hasPermission() denies when no policies exist — a silent reclassification that breaks core admin workflows at the V1→V2 cutover; the diff's own tests (testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient) only exercise the explicitly-granted path, never the admin-role path.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ClientPermissionsV2`, `canManage(ClientModel)` and other high-level checks explicitly bypass permission evaluation when the caller has `AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS` (e.g., `if (root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS)) return true;`). However, the role-mapping checks `canMapRoles(ClientModel)`, `canMapCompositeRoles(ClientModel)`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)` *only* call `hasPermission(client, <scope>)` and do not include any admin-role bypass. As implemented, `hasPermission(...)` returns `false` when there is no per-client resource and no policies on the type-level "all clients" resource (it explicitly checks `findByResource(...).isEmpty()` and returns `false`), so a user with only the realm role `MANAGE_CLIENTS` can be forbidden from client role-mapping operations in V2 unless explicit permissions are created. The added test `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` indeed only covers the explicit-permission path and does not cover the admin-role path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] canExchangeTo (lines 147-150), isPermissionsEnabled (187-190), resource (197-200), and getPermissions (202-205) replace the working inherited V1 implementations with throwing stubs, while in-tree callers that were served by the inherited V1 code before this PR wired MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() to the V2 class — the token-exchange permission check and the /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/managementPermissions endpoint — still invoke them. In realms where V2 dispatch is active, client token exchange and the client managementPermissions admin API that previously worked via the inherited V1 code now return HTTP 500 (UnsupportedOperationException); the PR keeps the public method signatures on ClientPermissionEvaluator but switches their behavior to throw, so live flows break with no update to their call sites and no test coverage in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly wires MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() to return the new ClientPermissionsV2 (MgmtPermissionsV2.java) and ClientPermissionsV2 overrides several inherited methods (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, etc.) to throw UnsupportedOperationException. This is a concrete compatibility hazard: any existing code paths that previously called these ClientPermissions APIs via MgmtPermissionsV2 will now fail at runtime. However, the diff does not show the alleged in-tree callers (/admin/.../managementPermissions or token-exchange checks) still invoking these methods, so the claim that HTTP 500s are definitively introduced cannot be verified from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new Clients resource type is registered in the V2 schema (line 68 and the super(Map.of(...)) at line 73) with no backfill, dual-read, or documented cutover for V1 fine-grained client permission data, which lives as 'client.<id>' resources under the permission client's resource server and is invisible to ClientPermissionsV2's findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()) lookups. A realm that already configured V1 per-client fine-grained permissions and then enables the V2 feature silently loses every existing client delegation at cutover — delegated admins get 403s with no error explaining why, the stale V1 rows sit permanently unread in the database, and operators must discover by hand that every grant has to be re-created against the new Clients type.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new CLIENTS resource type in AdminPermissionsSchema and ClientPermissionsV2 evaluates permissions by looking up a Resource named client.getId() (or falling back to the all-clients type resource). However, the finding’s core claim—that existing V1 fine-grained client permissions are stored as resources named like "client.<id>" and would therefore become invisible at V2 cutover—is not verifiable from this diff because no prior V1 client permission storage/naming logic or migration/cutover behavior is shown here. If V1 already used client IDs as resource names, V2 would still find them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ClientPermissionsV2 ships dead scaffolding: the private getEvaluationContext method (lines 262-272) has no caller because canExchangeTo throws instead of evaluating, and the static TOKEN_EXCHANGE import (line 46), the org.keycloak.authorization.model.Scope import (line 27), and the logger field (line 51) are unused in the file. The next maintainer implementing V2 token exchange inherits half-wired code whose presence implies exchange evaluation is already supported; roughly twenty lines and three imports are deletable now, and the unused logger signals intended error handling that was never written.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2` file, the `private static final Logger logger` field is declared but never referenced, the static import `AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE` is not referenced, and the import `org.keycloak.authorization.model.Scope` is not referenced anywhere in the class. Also, `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel authorizedClient, AccessToken token)` (near the end of the file) has no callers in this diff: all token-exchange related overrides (`canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, etc.) immediately throw `UnsupportedOperationException`, and no other method invokes `getEvaluationContext`. This is real dead/unused scaffolding grounded in the diff, but it’s not a runtime correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The ClientRemovedEvent branch calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which this same PR wires (MgmtPermissionsV2.clients(), lines 63-68) to ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled — a method this PR defines to unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException (ClientPermissionsV2.java:192-195) — so every client deletion in any deployment where the V2 evaluator is active (the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ-enabled configuration the handler's own gate at line 77 selects, and the configuration this PR's tests run under) throws inside the event listener. The provider event manager swallows and logs listener exceptions, so the delete itself succeeds but the authorization-resource cleanup the handler exists to perform silently never runs: every routine client delete logs an error-level UnsupportedOperationException stack trace and leaves an orphaned Clients-type resource in the authz store for the deleted client, which then resurfaces as a ghost ID in the findByType walks of getClientsWithPermission for a client that no longer exists.

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener(), when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled it handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). This PR changes MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() to return a new ClientPermissionsV2 instance (services/.../MgmtPermissionsV2.java), and ClientPermissionsV2 overrides setPermissionsEnabled(...) to unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException (services/.../ClientPermissionsV2.java). Therefore, in any configuration where management(...) resolves to MgmtPermissionsV2 while the listener gate is enabled, a client deletion event will trigger an exception in the listener instead of performing the intended cleanup/disable action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getClientsWithPermission's findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) walk also returns the all-clients type resource (the resource named "Clients" that hasPermission(String scope) at line 244 looks up by that exact name), and hasGrantedPermission returns true for it whenever the type-level permission grants the requested scope — so the literal string "Clients", which is not a client ID, is added to a set whose contract is client IDs (per-client resources are named by resolveClient with client.getId()). An admin holding an all-clients grant for a scope with no global short-circuit (e.g. map-roles or configure, where canView()/canManage() stay false) receives a granted set containing "Clients"; the consumer resolving it via clients().getClientById gets a null ClientModel and either NPEs (500 on the listing endpoint) or silently drops it and returns an empty/partial list despite the all-clients grant.
matched_golden_ids: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same core bug: getClientsWithPermission iterates resources returned by findByType(CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE), which includes the type-level "Clients" resource, and adds its name ("Clients") into a set that is supposed to contain actual client IDs. The downstream consumer then calls getClientById with this non-ID value, leading to null clients and failures/incorrect results. This matches the golden comment’s issue about type-level resources and returning resource.getName() instead of real client IDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] canExchangeTo unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException while the V1 method it replaces is a boolean grant/deny decision evaluated on the token-exchange request path (the AccessToken parameter and the ClientModelIdentity-based evaluation context — copied dead into this class at lines 262-272 — exist precisely to evaluate a source client's exchange grant at runtime). In any realm where the V2 evaluator is active, a cross-client token exchange that reaches the admin exchangeTo permission check fails with an unhandled UnsupportedOperationException — a raw 500 from the token endpoint instead of a grant or deny — breaking confidential-client token exchange under the feature with no fallback path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `ClientPermissionsV2` explicitly overrides `canExchangeTo(...)` (and multiple related permission methods) to always `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (e.g., around lines ~113-160 of the new file). It also contains a `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` helper that is unused, suggesting incomplete/leftover implementation. However, the finding’s claim that token-exchange requests will necessarily hit this method and produce an unhandled 500 cannot be verified from this diff alone (no call sites/control flow shown). So this is a concrete, diff-grounded concern about unimplemented functionality/potential runtime exception, but not a provable defect from the provided changeset alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The "evaluate resource and match granted scope" loop is hand-copied three times (lines 224-235, 249-260, and 276-286 — already drifting stylistically between expectedScopes.contains(s) and scope.equals(s)), and canManageClientScopes (lines 106-110) reimplements canManage() (lines 72-74) inline. The next change to scope-matching semantics (negative-logic grants, manage/configure-implies-view, scope renames) must be applied in four places in authorization-critical code; missing one copy yields different permission decisions between the per-client path, the type-level path, and the listing path — whoever maintains this pays the drift with silent misauthorization.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2`, the permission-evaluation + scope-matching logic is duplicated in multiple places: `hasPermission(ClientModel,String)` loops over `permissions` and checks `expectedScopes.contains(s)`, `hasPermission(String)` repeats the same pattern, and `hasGrantedPermission(Resource,String)` repeats it again but uses `scope.equals(s)` instead. This is diff-grounded and creates drift risk in authorization-critical code because future changes to how scopes are interpreted would need to be updated consistently across all copies. Additionally, `canManageClientScopes()` reimplements the same high-level check shape as `canManage(ClientModel)`/`canManage()` (admin-role short-circuit + `MANAGE` permission), rather than delegating, which further increases the number of places to maintain permission semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new class ships dead code: private getEvaluationContext has zero callers (canExchangeTo throws instead of using it), the logger field (line 51) is never used, and the static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE (line 46) plus the ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext/EvaluationContext imports exist only to serve the dead method. A future contributor wiring token exchange into V2 will find a ready-made, never-executed, never-tested evaluation-context builder and reuse it assuming it works, and the class carries a misleading compile dependency on V1's AdminPermissionManagement; the method, field, and imports delete cleanly (~12 lines plus 4 imports).

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2` class, the `logger` field is declared but never referenced, and the private `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` method has no callers in the diff (the only nearby related methods `canExchangeTo(...)`/`exchangeToPermission(...)` etc. all throw `UnsupportedOperationException`). The static import `AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE` is also unused, and the `ClientModelIdentity`/`DefaultEvaluationContext`/`EvaluationContext` imports appear to exist solely to support the unused `getEvaluationContext` method. This is diff-grounded cleanup/maintenance debt rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new feature gate skips the removal-time permission cleanup entirely whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is disabled, leaving no code path that ever deletes the stored permission resources of a realm that created fine-grained permissions while the feature was enabled and was later disabled. An operator who disables the preview feature accumulates one orphaned authorization resource per deleted client/role/group from that point on, and re-enabling the feature surfaces stale grants and policy-resource entries referencing entities that no longer exist.
matched_golden_ids: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core problem: permission cleanup on entity removal is incorrectly gated by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature flag, so when that flag is off the listener never runs and orphaned permission resources accumulate. While it doesn’t explicitly call out the V1 vs V2 inconsistency, it describes the same resulting bug (cleanup skipped due to the wrong/too-strict feature gate).
